rows.title: Open problem: Positive-temperature crystalline Gibbs phases for three-dimensional Riesz gases
rows.body:

rows.title: Attempt on Positive-temperature crystalline Gibbs phases for three-dimensional Riesz gases
rows.body:
ATTEMPT RECORD from the Codex campaign (author-checked by that worker only). Method: Source-specific calculation, conditional implication or exact obstruction Result: The harmonic phonon calculation around an assumed crystal has infrared displacement variance proportional to integral over |k|<1 of |k|^-2 dk. In dimension d this is a constant times integral from0 to1 of r^(d-3)dr, finite in d=3 and logarithmically divergent in d=2. Therefore the elementary infrared objection to positional order is absent in three dimensions. Check: The radial Jacobian r^(d-1) produces the exponent d-3. This only checks the Gaussian approximation conditional on a lattice; it neither selects a lattice nor constructs an infinite-volume Gibbs measure. Obstruction: One must control defects, anharmonic fluctuations and alternative configurations uniformly in volume and show nontrivial positional order. Finite variance within an assumed crystal cannot prove that the full Gibbs law is crystalline. Numerical BCC/FCC phase diagrams are not a proof.

rows.title: Convex Function and Its Subdifferential
rows.body: Let C be a convex subset of a real vector space X and f: C -> R. f is convex if f(lambda x + (1-lambda) y) <= lambda f(x) + (1-lambda) f(y) for all x, y in C and lambda in [0,1]. If X is a normed space with dual X*, the subdifferential of f at a point x_0 in C is the set partial f(x_0) = {v in X* : f(x) >= f(x_0) + v(x - x_0) for all x in C}, whose elements are called subgradients of f at x_0; partial f(x_0) may be empty, a single point, or contain more than one point. [standard, e.g. Rockafellar, Convex Analysis]

rows.title: First-Order Characterization of Convexity
rows.body:
A differentiable function f on an open convex set C is convex if and only if f(y) >= f(x) + <grad f(x), y - x> for all x, y in C: the graph lies above every tangent plane.
f differentiable on an open convex set

rows.title: Theorem 3.13 (Brascamp–Lieb inequality) of arXiv:2405.06616: Fast Mixing in Sparse Random Ising Models
rows.body: [Theorem 3.13 (Brascamp–Lieb inequality) of arXiv:2405.06616, 'Fast Mixing in Sparse Random Ising Models'] For any distribution with density ν ∝exp(−V) for some V : Rn →R, if there is a matrix Γ ≻0 such that ∇2V(z) ⪰Γ uniformly, then Cov(ν) ⪯Γ−1. Using the Hubbard-Stratonovich transform with the Brascamp-Lieb inequality allows us to bound covariances using the following lemma.
